title: Dia: Meet Dia
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: Dia's composer is lifted out of the window and floats alone on a painted sunburst, so each prompt ('Chat with your homework', 'Compare', 'Shorter, warmer…') reads as the subject; the window only appears at the very end. 24 s.
instrument: The measured pulls (×0.17–0.48) are the rising sun and the composer scaling in, content motion, not a camera.

byEye.zoom: the composer at about ×3 (its pill spans a third of the width); tab chips peek up from a strip of the tab bar at the bottom edge
byEye.cards: a small presenter line ('The Browser Company of New York'), the logo orb rising as a sun; no claim cards
byEye.frame: no window until the last shot; components float on a painted sunburst in Dia's palette
byEye.sound: an audio track with rhythmic onsets (not listened to)

curveFits.others: spring ζ=0.8 on linear scale, ω 3.2/s, 1180 ms (0.9%)

classify: Motion-designed launch film: the UI rebuilt as isolated, floating components on an illustrated backdrop. Conventions: a title sequence, a logo reveal, typed prompts, one wide shot of the real window at the end.

diagnose.observation: The composer floats alone, at three times its size.
diagnose.principle: Isolation: removing the window strips every competing element, so the input is the only thing to read.

diagnose.observation: The window is withheld until the last shot.
diagnose.principle: Delayed reveal: the viewer meets the behaviour before the product, then the window answers 'where is this'.
Crossfades read as the same place, different moment: time passes, the location doesn't.

teaches.text: Isolate the component: render one element's box alone on the backdrop at large scale.
Typing is the shot; the field is large.
Dissolves, not cuts, between beats that happen in the same place.

critique.like: The prompts are the script: you learn what Dia does from what's typed, with no claim cards at all.
critique.wish: Nothing shows a real page being read; the tab chips are the only link to the browser.
critique.wonder: Could cutscene screenshot a locator's box from the real app and float it on the backdrop, so isolation stays the real UI?
